rationale: The grain of the fact table. A null grain key means rows cannot be counted once.
A duplicated abstract double-counts a discharge, its cost, and its bed days — the single most expensive silent error in activity reporting.
An orphan facility key drops the row out of every site-level report while leaving the authority total intact — the totals still tie, so nobody notices.
An unmapped CMG has no RIW, so the case silently carries zero weight in cost per weighted case.
A stay of zero or negative days is a data-entry or timezone error, not a real admission.
ALC days are a subset of the stay and cannot be negative.
A zero or absent RIW makes cost per weighted case divide by something meaningless.
New disposition codes appear legitimately when a source system is upgraded. Worth knowing about, not worth halting month-end for.
A flag with a third value breaks every rate that divides by it.
The decomposition every bed-day figure depends on.
Discharged before admitted. Rare, and always a real defect.
Coding lag is normal in acute care; a stale extract is a service-level conversation with Health Information Management, not a pipeline defect.
Duplicate claims double-count both revenue and AR.
An orphan payer key hides a claim from every payer cut.
Status drives the entire adjudication and AR split.
